thread:
emma: Heads-up — seeing a regression on multi-GPU runs after we enabled CUDA graph capture for the forward+kv-prefetch path. All GPUs sit idle for ~50ms during the all-reduce step. Repro on canary.

kai: Which model/config? batch size, TP/PP, and are you seeing this only with graph capture? :eyes:

emma: batch=32, tp=2, pp=1, seq_len=2048, model=redwood/rwkv-13b-quant. Without graph capture overlap is fine. With capture -> throughput drops ~15-20%. We tried disabling KV prefetch and still see a hang.


david: Pasted an nsys snippet — shows big gap between kernel stream activity and NCCL launch:

```
Timeline:
  GPU0: kernel 0x1  (0-12ms)
  GPU0: cudaGraphLaunch (12-12.5ms)
  GPU0: idle (12.5-62ms)
  GPU0: ncclAllReduce launch (62ms)
```

And NVTX marks show cudaStreamWaitEvent before the allreduce.

emma: That wait event is suspicious — we schedule prefetch memcpy on stream A, then record event and wait on stream B inside the graph. During capture the event semantics seem to force serialization on replay.

kai: Are we capturing the memcpy + compute + allreduce inside one graph? Or are compute and comm captured separately and then launched?

emma: We capture forward+kv-prefetch as a single graph, then replay before calling ncclAllReduce on the default comm stream. The recorded graph contains stream waits to sync prefetch. On replay those wait events appear to block the comm stream until the whole graph finishes, losing overlap.


david: Also noticed kernel-selection fallback messages in the logs when seq_len>1536 — runtime picks fallback GEMM kernel with different stream affinity, might be changing launch order. Log extract: `kernel_select: fallback_matmul_fast -> generic_matmul_v2, stream=3`.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout detected performance regression, rolling back to previous build (rollback id: r-2026-04-12-08).

sre-oncall: Thanks infra-bot. Quick triage idea: try (A) disable graph capture for regions that touch inter-stream events, or (B) ensure prefetched memcpy and compute are recorded on the same stream used for comm to avoid event waits at replay. Which is easier to test?

emma: I tried (A) locally — skipping graph capture for the prefetch region restores overlap and we regain ~18% throughput.

kai: Good repro. For a long-term fix we probably need to change capture/layout logic so we don't insert cudaEvent-waits across streams into graphs that will be replayed concurrently with NCCL launches. Maybe prefer `cudaGraphAddMemcpyNode` tied to the comm stream or move prefetch to comm stream.


david: Filed issue perf#3421 with traces + nsys output + kernel selection logs. Attaching nvlink counters shows spikes in `PCIe Tx idle` during the delay.

emma: Can we also try forcing fused allreduce kernels (when available) during graph replay? If kernel selection picks a fused comm kernel that launches in the same stream context we might avoid the wait.

kai: Good call. Also need to add a unit test in the replay path that asserts no blocking cudaStreamWaitEvent between captured compute and an immediate NCCL launch.

emma: I'll add the minimal repro + test. Tagging @perf-team for follow-up and prioritization. :thumbsup:
